title: Batch One Is Too Sour  (第一批太酸了)

segments.t: 一号烤模刚出炉，咖啡角落里飘起金黄色的热气。亚瑟得意地把自制的柠檬糖釉刷在蛋糕表面，泰莎则递给格雷厄姆一把小叉子。请先仔细听一遍完整场景。
Stand back and admire Batch One — glazed personally by the owner of Linden Courtyard Inn!
You measured two small teaspoons of lemon juice plus sugar, right, Arthur?
Two big soup ladles of pure lemon juice for bold, unforgettable summer flavor!
Arthur! Soup ladles?! Where were your reading glasses when you read the spoon size?!
Wait — too late, Graham already put a full forkful into his mouth!
Give me one quiet moment while my cheeks try to unpucker themselves.
Here is a glass of cold water, Graham — what is your official pencil score?
The almond crumb is tender, the berries are sweet, and the top could polish brass.
Polish brass?! Surely a refreshing citrus zing deserves at least seven points!
I am writing three out of ten, plus a warning label for the front desk.
Thank you for your sacrifice, Judge; Arthur is officially retired from spoon duty!
Well! Wait until you see how crunchy Owen made Batch Number Two!
现在让我们一口一口——也就是逐句——来品尝这第一个实验蛋糕吧。
Stand back and admire Batch One — glazed personally by the owner of Linden Courtyard Inn!
“大家往后退一步，好好欣赏这第一批蛋糕——这可是菩提树庭院客栈老板亲自抹的糖釉！”亚瑟摆出一副大厨的架势展示作品。短语动词 stand back 意思是“往后退、让开空间”：
Stand back and admire Batch One
后面的 glazed personally by 是被动结构，由 by 引出动作的执行者。owner（老板、主人）读作 /ˈoʊnər/，里面的 w 不发音。
You measured two small teaspoons of lemon juice plus sugar, right, Arthur?
“亚瑟，你量了两小茶匙柠檬汁加糖，对吧？”泰莎隐约觉得不对劲，向他确认。在陈述句末尾加上 right?，就像中文里的“对吧？”或“是不是？”，不用改变句子语序。
two small teaspoons of lemon juice
teaspoon 是喝茶用的“茶匙”，而 tablespoon 是大得多的“汤匙”。plus 在数学和食谱里常用来表示“加上”。
Two big soup ladles of pure lemon juice for bold, unforgettable summer flavor!
“两大汤勺纯柠檬汁，打造浓郁难忘的夏日风味！”亚瑟毫不掩饰地承认自己放猛了料。ladle 指深口大汤勺，比普通勺子大得多：
Two big soup ladles
bold 本义是“大胆的”，用来形容味道时指“浓郁强烈的”。flavor 是美式拼写，英式写作 flavour。unforgettable 由前缀 un-、forget 和后缀 -able 组成。
Arthur! Soup ladles?! Where were your reading glasses when you read the spoon size?!
“亚瑟！大汤勺！？你看勺子刻度的时候老花镜戴哪儿去了！？”泰莎简直不敢相信。reading glasses 是“老花镜（阅读眼镜）”，动词加 -ing 放在名词前说明用途。
when you read the spoon size?!
注意读音：这里第二个 read 是过去式，读作 /rɛd/，和红色 red 同音，只是拼写和原形一样。
Wait — too late, Graham already put a full forkful into his mouth!
“等等——太晚了，格雷厄姆已经把满满一叉子蛋糕塞进嘴里了！”惨剧已经来不及阻止了。后缀 -ful 能把容器变成计量单位，forkful 是“一叉子的量”，类似的还有 spoonful 和 handful。
put a full forkful into his mouth!
put 的原形、过去式和过去分词拼写读音完全相同。留意这里说的是 his mouth，英语习惯加上物主代词“他的嘴”。
Give me one quiet moment while my cheeks try to unpucker themselves.
“给我一点安静的时间，让我的脸颊试着自己舒展开来。”柠檬的酸劲让格雷厄姆五官都皱在了一起。pucker 是“皱起、撅起”，格雷厄姆幽默地在前面加上否定前缀 un- 造了个反义词：
try to unpucker themselves.
themselves 是复数反身代词，指代前面的 cheeks（脸颊）。另外，cheek 作单数用时，口语里还有“厚脸皮、没大没小”的意思。
Here is a glass of cold water, Graham — what is your official pencil score?
“格雷厄姆，给你一杯冷水——用铅笔写下的官方评分是多少？”泰莎一边递水救急，一边追问结果。把东西递给别人时，Here is 相当于“给你、拿着”：
a glass of cold water,
glass 可以指“玻璃杯”，也可以指“玻璃”；“眼镜（glasses）”这个词就来源于此。score 是“分数”，前面的 pencil 用来修饰它，指“铅笔写的评分”。
The almond crumb is tender, the berries are sweet, and the top could polish brass.
“杏仁蛋糕体松软细腻，浆果香甜可口，至于表面嘛，拿去擦黄铜都够格。”格雷厄姆先扬后抑，来了句冷幽默。crumb 是“蛋糕屑、蛋糕体”，结尾的 b 不发音，和 lamb、thumb 一样。
and the top could polish brass.
这里的 could 表示可能性，“拿去……都行”。polish 作动词是“擦亮、抛光”；注意首字母大写的 Polish 则是“波兰的、波兰语”。
Polish brass?! Surely a refreshing citrus zing deserves at least seven points!
“擦黄铜！？这么提神的柑橘风味，起码也值七分吧！”亚瑟不服气地为自己的糖釉辩护。surely 在这里不表示“当然”，而是带着惊讶和反问的语气，希望对方能认同自己。
a refreshing citrus zing
zing 是一个很有画面感的词，形容鲜明提神的风味或活力。at least 意思是“至少、起码”。
I am writing three out of ten, plus a warning label for the front desk.
“我写下十分中的三分，外加一张贴给前台的警示标签。”裁判铁面无私。表达“几分之几的评分”时，英语用 out of（three out of ten）。
three out of ten,
warning label 是“警示标签”，warning 来自 warn（警告）。在 front desk 里，desk 不是“办公桌”，而是酒店旅馆的“前台接待台”。
Thank you for your sacrifice, Judge; Arthur is officially retired from spoon duty!
“谢谢你做出牺牲，裁判先生；亚瑟正式从管勺子的差事中退休了！”泰莎果断又幽默地下了决定。retired 是“退休的”，后面用介词 from 引出退出的工作：
officially retired from spoon duty!
duty 意思是“职责、差事、值班”。注意 sacrifice 最后一个音节的元音发 /aɪ/，读作 /ˈsækrɪfaɪs/。
Well! Wait until you see how crunchy Owen made Batch Number Two!
“好吧！等着瞧吧，看看欧文把第二批做得有多脆！”亚瑟有点挂不住面子，立刻岔开了话题。Wait until you see 是用来吊人胃口的常用句型，相当于“等着瞧吧”：
Wait until you see
后面的 how crunchy 表示“有多脆”。make + 宾语 + 形容词表示“使某物变成某种状态”，如 made it crunchy（把它做得很脆）。最后，请不受打扰地再听一遍完整场景。
Stand back and admire Batch One — glazed personally by the owner of Linden Courtyard Inn!
You measured two small teaspoons of lemon juice plus sugar, right, Arthur?
Two big soup ladles of pure lemon juice for bold, unforgettable summer flavor!
Arthur! Soup ladles?! Where were your reading glasses when you read the spoon size?!
Wait — too late, Graham already put a full forkful into his mouth!
Give me one quiet moment while my cheeks try to unpucker themselves.
Here is a glass of cold water, Graham — what is your official pencil score?
The almond crumb is tender, the berries are sweet, and the top could polish brass.
Polish brass?! Surely a refreshing citrus zing deserves at least seven points!
I am writing three out of ten, plus a warning label for the front desk.
Thank you for your sacrifice, Judge; Arthur is officially retired from spoon duty!
Well! Wait until you see how crunchy Owen made Batch Number Two!
两大汤勺纯柠檬汁，让第一批蛋糕只拿到了三分，还附带格雷厄姆一句“小心腐蚀黄铜”的警告。再见，祝你今天愉快！
Goodbye!
